newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH CALL MONEY REMAINS UNDER UPWARD PRESSURE.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH CALL MONEY REMAINS UNDER UPWARD PRESSURE.

text.p: Dutch call money rose a little further on Thursday but dealers said the rate could slip again when a new special advances pact kicks in on Friday.
"Of course it will all depend on the size of the new allocation, but call money has been under quite some upward pressure under the current pact," said one dealer.
Dealers said the rate on special advances, currently pegged at 2.50 percent, was likely to remain unchanged.
The Dutch central bank is due to set a new pact at 1500 GMT.
Earlier, Germany's Bundesbank said after its fortnightly meeting it would hold its key discount and Lombard rates steady.
Market players said they had not been expecting any changes in official rates in Germany.
Call money rates were bid as high as 2.87 percent in thin trade. On Wednesday call money was bid at 2.75 or higher.
Money market dealers said the auction of Nederlandsche Bank Certificates (NBCs) on November 26 -- between 0900-1000 GMT -- could raise about 1.4 billion guilders.
The Dutch central bank said 1.5 billion guilders was a maximum.
NBCs are interest-bearing negotiable certificates issued to drain structural money market surpluses. They are issued at monthly auctions, with a maturity of six months.
The guilder was unchanged versus the German mark at 112.165 per 100 marks.
